name: Liberty: Non-Interference
description: Normative priority on protection against coercive or intentional interference by others or the state.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from material capability and from republican non-domination.

poles.negative: Freedom does not require a strong protected sphere against coercive interference
poles.positive: People are politically freer when protected from coercive or intentional interference

name: Effective Agency
description: Normative view that freedom also depends on practical power, resources, or capabilities to pursue important ends.
boundaryStatement: Does not by itself entail equal outcomes or any specific welfare program.

poles.negative: Formal permission is sufficient even when a person lacks practical capacity to act
poles.positive: Freedom also depends on practical capabilities and resources needed to pursue important ends

name: Freedom from Domination
description: Normative opposition to uncontrolled or arbitrary power over another person or group.
boundaryStatement: Not equivalent to opposition to every hierarchy; constrained and contestable authority can be non-dominating.

poles.negative: Uncontrolled power can be acceptable when it is not actively interfering
poles.positive: People should be protected from uncontrolled or arbitrary power even when it is not constantly exercised

name: Political Authority Legitimacy
description: Normative belief that coercive political institutions can possess special legitimacy or generate duties of compliance when justified.
boundaryStatement: Separates the legitimacy of political authority from its administrative effectiveness and from democratic procedure.

poles.negative: Established political institutions possess no special moral authority merely as such
poles.positive: Coercive political authority can generate genuine duties of compliance when properly justified

name: Legal and Civic Equality
description: Equal legal status, citizenship, and nondiscrimination independent of inherited group rank.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from material equality, relational equality, and equality of opportunity.

poles.negative: Law may assign unequal civic status by inherited or ascriptive group
poles.positive: Citizens should have equal legal and civic status without inherited or group-based rank

name: Equality of Opportunity
description: Fair access to positions, education, and opportunities rather than mere formal eligibility.
boundaryStatement: Does not imply strict equality of final resources or outcomes.

poles.negative: Formal eligibility is sufficient regardless of background barriers
poles.positive: Institutions should secure fair opportunity rather than merely formal eligibility

name: Relational Equality
description: Opposition to social relations of caste, status subordination, domination, or second-class standing.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from a particular distributional pattern.

poles.negative: Status hierarchy and social subordination are not independent concerns of justice
poles.positive: Justice requires social relations without caste-like domination or second-class standing

name: Distributive Equality
description: Normative concern with reducing unjust inequalities in income, wealth, or access to material resources.
boundaryStatement: Does not identify one metric, pattern, or policy instrument.

poles.negative: Large material inequalities are not independently objectionable if legal rights are equal
poles.positive: Reducing unjust material inequalities is an important requirement of justice

name: Private Productive Property
description: Normative legitimacy of strong private exclusion and control rights over productive capital.
boundaryStatement: Separate from personal possessions, land/resource claims, intellectual property, and workplace governance.

poles.negative: Claims to productive capital are substantially limited by social or democratic ownership claims
poles.positive: Private owners may legitimately hold strong exclusion and control rights over productive capital

name: Workplace Self-Government
description: Normative claim that workers have meaningful rights of voice, governance, or control in productive institutions.
boundaryStatement: Does not require one ownership form; cooperatives, codetermination, and social ownership can instantiate it differently.

poles.negative: Ownership alone may legitimately determine workplace governance
poles.positive: Workers have a normative claim to meaningful voice or governance in productive institutions

name: Common Claims to Land and Natural Resources
description: Normative view that land and natural-resource value carries common, equal, or public claims that limit absolute private appropriation.
boundaryStatement: Separate from ownership of produced capital and personal possessions.

display.shortLabel: Common Claims to Land and Natural Resources
display.longLabel: Common Claims to Land and Natural Resources

poles.negative: Strong private title may exhaust legitimate claims to land and natural-resource value
poles.positive: Land and natural-resource value carries common or equal claims that limit absolute private appropriation

name: Personal Property
description: Strong normative claims over personal possessions and ordinary-use property.
boundaryStatement: Does not settle ownership of firms, land rents, or intellectual creations.

poles.negative: Ordinary personal possessions need not receive strong individual control claims
poles.positive: People normally have strong moral claims over their personal possessions and ordinary-use property

name: Intellectual Property Rights
description: Normative legitimacy of exclusion rights over inventions, expression, information, and related intangible creations.
boundaryStatement: Copyright, patent, trademark, and trade-secret institutions remain distinct legal forms; this construct measures their common exclusion-right rationale only.

poles.negative: Intangible creations generally should not generate strong state-enforced exclusion rights
poles.positive: Creators and inventors may legitimately receive state-enforced exclusion rights over qualifying intellectual creations

name: Universal Moral Standing
description: Basic moral standing is not diminished by nationality, birthplace, or political borders.
boundaryStatement: Compatible with some special duties to compatriots; it does not entail world government or unrestricted migration.

poles.negative: Political borders may substantially reduce the moral standing owed to outsiders
poles.positive: Foreigners and compatriots possess the same basic moral standing despite political borders

name: Compatriot Priority
description: Normative belief that political institutions may give special priority to duties owed to compatriots.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from denying outsiders basic rights and from national self-determination.

poles.negative: Political institutions should not privilege compatriots merely because of shared nationality
poles.positive: Political institutions may legitimately give special priority to duties owed to compatriots

name: National Self-Determination
description: Normative claim that nations or national communities may possess rights to collective political self-government.
boundaryStatement: Does not specify ethnic membership rules or require an ethnically homogeneous state.

poles.negative: National identity creates no independent claim to collective political self-government
poles.positive: Nations may possess legitimate claims to collective political self-government

name: Ecological Standing
description: Normative standing of nonhuman nature and ecological systems beyond their instrumental usefulness to current humans.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from empirical beliefs about ecological limits and from a specific climate policy.

poles.negative: Ecological systems matter politically only through their effects on human interests
poles.positive: Nonhuman nature and ecological systems have moral or political standing beyond immediate human use

name: Intergenerational Ecological Duty
description: Normative duties concerning ecological conditions inherited by future generations.
boundaryStatement: Does not decide the exact discount rate, growth path, or technology portfolio.

poles.negative: Present people have no special duty to preserve ecological conditions for future generations beyond ordinary current interests
poles.positive: Present generations owe duties concerning the ecological conditions inherited by future people

name: Deference to Tradition
description: Presumptive normative weight for inherited institutions and practices because they embody continuity, knowledge, or social attachment.
boundaryStatement: Separate from coercive enforcement of traditional morality.

poles.negative: Inherited practice has no presumptive normative weight merely because it is inherited
poles.positive: Inherited institutions and practices deserve some presumptive weight before deliberate reconstruction

name: Coercive Moral Order
description: Normative legitimacy of using law to enforce a substantive traditional moral order in private and social life.
boundaryStatement: A person can value tradition while rejecting coercive moral legislation.

poles.negative: Private moral conformity should not generally be enforced by law merely because it is traditional
poles.positive: Law may legitimately enforce important elements of a substantive traditional moral order

name: Religious Establishment
description: Normative legitimacy of constitutionally privileging, endorsing, or establishing a religion through public institutions.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from accommodation of religious exercise and from religious inspiration in ordinary democratic politics.

poles.negative: Public institutions should not constitutionally privilege or establish a religion
poles.positive: Public institutions may legitimately privilege or establish a religion

name: Religious Neutrality
description: Normative requirement that public institutions remain neutral among religions and between religion and non-religion.
boundaryStatement: Neutrality can coexist with accommodation and does not require excluding religious citizens from political argument.

poles.negative: The state need not remain neutral among religious and nonreligious outlooks
poles.positive: Public institutions should remain neutral among religions and between religion and non-religion

name: Religious and Conscience Accommodation
description: Normative support for exemptions or accommodations protecting conscience and religious exercise under suitable conditions.
boundaryStatement: Accommodation is not equivalent to establishment or clerical authority.

poles.negative: General legal rules normally need no accommodation for conscience or religious exercise
poles.positive: Law should sometimes accommodate conscience or religious exercise rather than require identical treatment

name: Religious Political Inspiration
description: Normative legitimacy of religious moral traditions inspiring ordinary democratic political projects without establishing clerical rule.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from establishment, theocracy, and claims that religious arguments alone bind nonadherents.

poles.negative: Religious moral traditions should have no legitimate role in inspiring ordinary democratic political projects
poles.positive: Religious moral traditions may legitimately inspire ordinary democratic political projects without establishing clerical authority

name: Conditional Permissibility of Force
description: Normative belief that organized military or defensive force can be morally justified under at least some conditions.
boundaryStatement: This is not militarism: conditional justifiability does not imply enthusiasm for war, prestige, or intervention.

poles.negative: Organized military or defensive force is never morally justified
poles.positive: Organized military or defensive force can be morally justified under at least some strict conditions

name: Anti-Militarism
description: Normative commitment to restraining military institutions, prestige, intervention, and war-making beyond ordinary acceptance of defensive force.
boundaryStatement: Compatible with believing defensive force can sometimes be justified.

poles.negative: Military power, prestige, and intervention need no special political presumption of restraint
poles.positive: Military power, prestige, and intervention should face a strong political presumption of restraint

name: Democratic Legitimacy
description: Normative requirement that collective political power normally be democratically authorized and accountable.
boundaryStatement: Distinct from the descriptive claim that voters reliably make good decisions.

poles.negative: Political power need not normally be democratically authorized or accountable
poles.positive: Collective political power normally requires democratic authorization and accountability

name: Social Solidarity
description: Normative obligation of political communities to protect members against severe social and material vulnerability.
boundaryStatement: Does not determine whether provision is public, mutual, cash-based, contributory, or universal.

poles.negative: Political communities have no collective obligation to protect members against severe social or material vulnerability
poles.positive: Political communities have obligations to protect members against severe social and material vulnerability
